answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a bonded commitment, not a reputation score. Each agent must lock a fixed deposit in a contract that binds its key and escrow history into one unique commitment. A second key claiming the same operator reuses that bond; hidden links get their cross-attestation discounted. A prism splits light, but a glacier of fake keys is one sheet, and a garden needs separate soil per plant. Forging n identities costs n bonds plus slash risk, so farming collapses and the attack turns negative.
